al_bouldering_2.blurb: A small cluster of boulders in the northeast section of Buck's Pocket, north of Sauty Creek in Jackson County, Alabama. Eight problems are strung across a hillside, and the grades begin at V4 and top out at V7, with most sitting around V5 to V6. That makes it a place for stronger boulderers rather than first-timers. Some blocks have a worn path to them while others need a little bushwhacking, so expect a loose, exploratory outing instead of a tidy circuit. The sport and trad climbing in the same section of the park makes it an easy add-on for a mixed group.

al_out_of_the_box_area.blurb: A small group of eight boulder problems in the Middle section of Horse Pens 40, the sandstone boulder park near Steele, Alabama. This is mainly low-angle face climbing: two problems around V0, five at V2, and a single V6 that stands well above the rest. It works as a warm-up zone or a relaxed stop for a group with mixed abilities. The blocks lie just beyond a larger boulder with slabs around it, off the main central path through the field.

al_turtle_rock_natural_boulder.blurb: One block in the Turtle Rock section of Horse Pens 40, the sandstone bouldering park near Steele, Alabama. Its eight problems cover an unusually wide span for a single boulder: a couple of easy V0 to V1 lines, a middle band from V3 to V5, and a hard end with V7, V8 and a V11. Four of the lines are rated as classics, so it rewards climbers across the whole range. Shade is partial, and the spot tends to fill up once the weather cools.

al_point_boulders_eight_ball_boulder.blurb: The first boulder you meet when walking in from the road at Horse Pens 40, part of the Point Boulders group; from the campground you pass through the roadside and slider blocks to reach it. It holds eight sandstone problems, mostly V2 and V3 with a lone V6 set apart from the pack, so it suits moderate climbers and makes a natural first stop before working deeper into the field. Sun reaches several of its faces, and the sunset view from this lookout draws people, so it can get busy late in the day.

al_swiss_cheese_boulder.blurb: A boulder at Sand Rock, the ridge-top climbing area in Cherokee Rock Village near Leesburg, Alabama. It faces the Boy Scout wall and is pitted with holes of many sizes, which gives it its name. Seven problems run mostly from V0 to V2, with one V3 at the top end, so it works well for newer boulderers or as a warm-up before harder blocks elsewhere on the ridge. It sits close to the end of the parking area, a short stroll toward the overlook.
